description: Table 4 is a rendered text table (no axes, no micrograph, no scale bar), laid out as five rows by four data columns, headed by "Engineering strain (%)". The four columns correspond to engineering strains of 3.0, 10.0, 20.0 and 28.0 %. Row 1 gives the corresponding "True strain, %": 3.0, 9.5, 18.2 and 24.7. Row 2 gives "True stress, MPa": 528, 662, 829 and 924. Row 3 gives the α-phase strengthening contribution "σ(α)(ε), MPa": 41, 104, 260 and 347. Row 4 gives the γ-phase contribution "σ(γ)(ε), MPa": 28, 67, 79 and 111. The table is the quantitative companion to the flow-stress decomposition plotted in Fig. 9(b) for 8Al steel, computed with Eqs. (5)–(8) from the data of Fig. 6; the citing text states that the best fit between calculation and experiment is obtained at this Al level. The values show both contributions rising monotonically with strain, with σ(α)(ε) increasing from 41 to 347 MPa (roughly an eightfold rise, and overtaking σ(γ)(ε) at every strain level), while σ(γ)(ε) grows only from 28 to 111 MPa, so that the α-phase (ferrite) term dominates the strain-hardening contribution to the flow stress as strain accumulates.

subfigures.description: Single rendered table (5 rows x 4 data columns) headed "Engineering strain (%)" with columns 3.0, 10.0, 20.0, 28.0; rows list True strain (%), True stress (MPa), σ(α)(ε) (MPa) and σ(γ)(ε) (MPa) for 8Al steel.

observations.observation: The table has four data columns corresponding to engineering strains of 3.0, 10.0, 20.0 and 28.0 %.
True strain values listed are 3.0, 9.5, 18.2 and 24.7 %, paired with the four engineering strains.
True stress values listed are 528, 662, 829 and 924 MPa, rising monotonically with strain.
The σ(α)(ε) strengthening contribution is 41, 104, 260 and 347 MPa at the four strain levels.
The σ(γ)(ε) strengthening contribution is 28, 67, 79 and 111 MPa at the four strain levels.
σ(α)(ε) exceeds σ(γ)(ε) in every column, and the gap widens with strain (41 vs 28 MPa at the lowest strain, 347 vs 111 MPa at the highest).
The caption states the table reports the strengthening contribution of σ(α)(ε) and σ(γ)(ε) to the flow stress.
The citing text states the values are calculated using Eqs. (5)-(8) and the data of Fig. 6, and compared with measured flow stress σ_tot shown in Table 4 and Fig. 9(b).
The citing text states the best fit between calculation and experiment is achieved for the 8Al steel; the table itself does not print the alloy label.
Neither the arithmetic sum σ(α)+σ(γ) nor any total flow-stress column is printed in the table; only the two phase contributions and the measured true stress are tabulated.
